title: Shadow-ledger reconciliation for stale reserved quota during pool rebalancing
creator: Asha Raman
description: Background: During reserved-capacity pool rebalances (scale-ups, preempt migrations, region failovers) we observed transient discrepancies between the primary quota ledger (live token counters used for rate limiting) and downstream billing/usage ledgers. Symptoms include: tenants briefly seeing consumed quota that isn't reflected in the billing ledger, transient over- or under-throttling, and manual support tickets asking for reconciliations. Root cause analysis points to partially-applied reservation operations, duplicative decrement attempts during request retries, and eventual-consistency delays between the write path and the archival usage ledger.
goals: 1) Provide an idempotent reconciliation mechanism ("shadow-ledger" pattern) to detect and repair stale reserved quota after pool rebalances; 2) Guarantee at-most-once consumption semantics for reserved pools where possible; 3) Emit clear telemetry and an automated runbook for on-call to remediate; 4) Minimize disruption during rollout and maintain billing correctness for downstream invoice generation.
acceptance_criteria: - Reconciliation job can detect >99.99% of ledger mismatches in synthetic workloads; - Repaired accounts converge to correct balances within 10 minutes after a rebalance event in 95th percentile; - No customer-visible double-debits in canary; - End-to-end integration test covering partial-write, retry storms, and tombstone cleanup.
technical_summary: Design: introduce a write-side shadow ledger (per-reservation microjournal) that records reservation intents and final outcome (applied/compensated) with monotonic operation IDs. During normal operation, reservation flow writes (1) decrement to live counter, (2) append intent to shadow journal, (3) ack to client. If any of these steps fail mid-flight, the shadow ledger allows a deterministic repair: a reconciliation worker compares shadow journal entries against the canonical billing ledger and live counters and emits compensating credits or replays missing decrements.
detailed_design_decisions: - Use existing durable KV (usage-ledger-store) namespaced per-tenant for the shadow journal to leverage retention and tombstone semantics; - Operation IDs are a 128-bit UUID + source-shard epoch to avoid collisions across rebalances; - Idempotency: reconciliation workers use compare-and-swap on a per-op marker to ensure a repair is applied once; - Backfill window: reconcile last 7 days by default, configurable per-tenant; - Reconciliation batch size tuned to tenant cardinality and reserved pool size to avoid thundering herds.
tradeoffs: - Pros: deterministic repair path, improved billing correctness, reduced manual tickets. - Cons: increased write path latency (~4-8ms median) due to additional append, additional storage cost for shadow entries, and complexity in rollout. We chose append-only shadow journal (vs. synchronous transactional writes) to keep live-path latency predictable and avoid coupling to the archival ledger write latency.
migration_and_rollout: Phased rollout: 1) Canary new shadow writes for 5 reserved pools (internal customers) with reconciliation disabled; 2) Enable reconciliation in read-only monitoring mode for next 48 hours and validate detection telemetry; 3) Enable auto-repair in canary; 4) Gradually expand to 25% of reserved capacity pools; 5) Full rollout with monitoring gates. Feature flag: 'shadow_reconciliation_v1' with emergency kill switch. Runbook pages and alerting included in next section.
telemetry_and_alerting: New metrics: shadow_journal_append_latency_ms, shadow_journal_entries_created, reconciliation_detected_mismatch_count, reconciliation_repairs_applied, reconciliation_time_to_converge_ms. Alerts: P0 if reconciliation_repairs_applied spikes > 1000/min or if time_to_converge 95p > 30m. Dashboards: 'Reserved Pool Quota Integrity' on Grafana (link below).
testing_plan: - Unit tests for idempotent repair logic; - Integration test simulating mid-flight failures and retries; - Chaos test: simulate shard rebalances and network partitions; - Load test: synthetic tenants with high reservation churn to validate throughput; - Billing integration test ensuring archival ledger matches repaired live counters.
rollback_plan: Feature flag off disables new shadow writes and stops automatic repairs. If rollback after repairs applied is required, run compensating migration to recompute canonical balances from billing ledger snapshots and tombstones using the 'reverse_repair' utility. Conservative approach: treat billing ledger as source-of-truth if uncertainty exists and issue customer-facing credits instead of aggressive reverse debits.
runbook: - On alert (mismatch spike): 1) Check 'Reserved Pool Quota Integrity' dashboard; 2) Validate recent rebalance events in cluster-ops; 3) Run reconciler dry-run for tenant subset; 4) If false positives, disable auto-repair and triage; 5) If real, monitor repairs_applied and verify downstream billing ledger ingestion. Escalation: on persistent >1h convergence, page SRE + Billing lead.
implementation_notes: - PR 7892 introduces the shadow journal shim and reconciler skeleton; follow-up PR will add idempotent CAS markers and backfill job. - Use existing job-queue infra (kafka topic 'reconcile-intents') for worker fanout. - Ensure GC policy for shadow entries: compact with tombstone after 90 days or when billing snapshot includes ops.
